title: The bird and the crow
logline: The seawall: the crow at one end, the bird at the other. Both looking at the water. The crow is real; the bird is not explained; the page treats them the same.

panels.composition: The seawall's full length across the page: at the left end, a crow; at the right end, the rainbow bird. Both facing the bay. Between them, the wall, and a long gray May afternoon.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a long concrete seawall across the page with a black crow at the left end and a small rainbow-colored bird at the right end both facing a gray bay, no words

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards
